verdict.rationale: Sift documents sending your own data: user lifecycle events via the REST Events API, custom events and fields for actions outside the supported schema, a JS snippet and mobile SDKs for client-side data, and historical backfill because the model 'gets smarter the more data it has about your business.' Device fingerprinting is not explicitly documented as a signal you control, and the evidence does not show how your custom fields change scores, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: explicit documentation of device-fingerprint collection or ingestion, explicit confirmation that custom fields feed the scoring model, independent hands-on corroboration that customer signals change scores.

support.subject: As a developer, I can feed the model my own signals — device fingerprints, behavioral data, custom metadata — so scoring reflects my business, not just network defaults

citations.quote: Custom events and fields describe user actions not captured by the supported events in our Events API.
Because Sift gets smarter the more data it has about your business, you can jump start your integration by backfilling a few months worth of historical data.
Sift easily integrates into your existing systems using modern REST APIs, Javascript snippet, and SDKs for iOS and Android.
You will send this data from your application to Sift via our REST API.
